correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the projective gradient exhaustion. If x=y=0, the two last derivatives exclude zw≠0 and z=0, leaving only P at t=0. With exactly one of x,y zero, the other derivative forces z=w≠0 and then t=1 and one of the two quartic equations at w/z=1. With xy≠0, z=w=0 is excluded by F_z+F_w=−12x²y². The first two derivatives then require h=(z−w)/(z+w) with h²=−3 and x²=−hy², ruling out zw=0. The mixed quartic terms cancel in F, forcing t=1 at w/z=ρ a primitive cube root. In z=1, F_w gives y⁴=−(1+ρ)/4=ρ²/4, and F_z vanishes with these substitutions. This gives 4+4+8+8 points. Independently evaluated the Hessian: at the two axial families it has determinant 3456. Off-axis, write B=1+ρ; H_xx=24By², H_xy/H_xx=−x/y, and the leading 2×2 block has determinant zero. The full determinant is −H_xx(H_yw+(x/y)H_xw)² with the squared term’s argument 24(1+h)y³. This simplifies to 3456ρ², so all points are nodes. At P the homogeneous leading quartic has no projective gradient zero; blowing up gives smooth strict transform along the exceptional genus-three quartic, with E²=−4 and discrepancy 2−4=−2. The smooth tangent cone gives the ordinary multiplicity-four Milnor number 3³=27. A smooth quintic has Euler number 55, and smoothing increases it by the sum of local Milnor numbers on a complex surface; the claimed values 28 and 31 follow. Homogenizing in the base gives the stated nonreduced fiber at infinity.
